Subject: Recap & next steps — pilot velocity + pricing

Hi Ava,

Great to speak this morning — thanks for the time. Quick written recap and concrete next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of what we covered
- Pilot scope: integrating Redwood inference into Northbridge’s triage pipeline for clinical-coding assistant (3-week pilot).
- Expected token profile: 5–7M tokens/week (peak days up to ~3M tokens). Tokens are mainly short prompts + ~80 token completions.
- Target unit economics you mentioned: target $/1M tokens in the low-mid hundreds (you cited ~$600 per 1M tokens as a target).
- Budget constraint: you flagged an internal pilot budget ~ $20k.

Our asks / proposed support from Redwood
- Apply temporary free credits to cover initial spike while you validate results.
- Set a conservative daily cap & alerting so we don’t exceed the internal budget unexpectedly.
- Provide SOC2 & data-retention summary for procurement.

Concrete next steps
1) I’ll confirm what level of free credits we can apply and any guardrails (token caps / alerts).
2) Monica will package the SOC2 summary and data deletion policy (attachment).
3) You confirm final pilot dates and whether procurement needs a PO or SOW.
4) Schedule a 10-day check-in during the pilot to review burn rate and quality metrics.

Attachments: pilot-MAP.pdf (proposed mutual action plan)

If you can confirm the pilot start date (we penciled June 1 in the call), we’ll lock the credits and guardrails.

Thanks —
Markus Klein

From: Ava Collins <ava.collins@northbridgehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — pilot velocity + pricing

Thanks Markus — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side before we proceed: 

1) Budget: the $20k pilot budget is firm (covers all software + internal validation work). We can stretch a little if Redwood provides credits that are strictly for inference spend. Ideally credits cover any spike above our planned consumption so the PO covers base consumption.

2) Volumes: our engineering lead says 5M tokens/week is reasonable, but there’s a risk of a 1–2 day spike during synthetic load tests that could push us to ~4–5M in a single day.

3) Unit economics: $600 per 1M tokens is the hopeful target, but procurement needs to see a comparison of estimated monthly run-rate at that price vs a stretched price (e.g., $750/1M).

4) Security/Compliance: please send SOC2, data deletion policy, and confirmation on whether logs contain PHI by default.

Procurement will need either a PO referencing Redwood’s standard terms or a short SOW — I’ll confirm which by Monday. For credits: if you can put a credit safety net in place (amount + expiry + caps), we’ll be comfortable running the load tests.

Ava Collins
Head of Clinical AI | Northbridge Health
ava.collins@northbridgehealth.com | +1 617-555-0188
